newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-DUTCH CRUISE TO COMFORTABLE WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUTCH CRUISE TO COMFORTABLE WIN.

text.p: Two long-range goals earned the Netherlands a comfortable 2-0 win over South Africa in a friendly on Wednesday.
The Dutch, without their contingent of Ajax players, kept comfortable possession and played at almost half pace against an experimental home team.
Giovanni van Bronkhorst scored in the eighth minute with a 20-metre shot that caught debutant goalkeeper Brian Baloyi unawares.
Jean-Paul van Gastel drove in the second in similar circumstances midway through the second half to effectively end the match.

South Africa, who have a vital World Cup qualifier against Zambia on Sunday, rested all but two of their regular starting line-up, leaving only captain Lucas Radebe and defender Neil Tovey in the team.
Mark Williams, returning after a six-month lay-off, missed a chance in the first 10 minutes and Helman Mkhalele ballooned a shot over the top with an open goal staring at him.
Dutch coach Gus Hiddink had much to be pleased about with his makeshift team. Wim Jonk and Aron Winter were outstanding in midfield.

South Africa - 20-Brian Baloyi; 19-Lucas Radebe, 4-Andrew Rabutla (5-Gavin Lane 81), 9-Neil Tovey; 6-Clinton Larsen (18-Brandon Silent 72), 7-Thomas Madigage (14-Thabo Mooki 63), 22-Dumisani Ngobe (3-Bradley Carnell 86), 8-Linda Buthelezi, 1-Helman Mkhalele; 12-Mark Williams (17-Benedict McCarthy 72), 13-George Koumantarakis (21-Pollen Ndlanya 46).

Netherlands - 1-Ed de Goey; 2-Michael Reiziger (12-Jean-Paul van Gastel 58), 3-Freddy Vierklau, 4-Phillip Cocu, 5-Arthur Numan; 6-Wim Jonk, 7-Aron Winter, 8-Giovanni van Bronkhorst, 10-Clarence Seedorf (13-Johan de Kock 68), 11-Boudewijn Zenden (15-Roy Makaay 81); 9-John Bosman (14-Pierre van Hooijdonk 68).
